```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Models and source

Qi 2026 built a one-compartment dynamic dilution model that reproduces the
urine concentrations of nemonoxacin after oral 500 mg once daily, challenged
*Escherichia coli* isolates in two media -- cation-adjusted Mueller-Hinton
broth (CAMHB) and synthetic human urine (SHU, pH 6.5) -- and related the
bacterial response over 24 h to six PK/PD indices with the sigmoid Emax model

E = E0 - Emax * X^H / (X^H + EC50^H)

where X is the index and E is either the change in log10 CFU/mL between 0 and
24 h (Delta log10 CFU) or the area under the log10 CFU/mL bacterial kill curve
over 0-24 h (AUBKC). Table 2 reports 17 independent fits; all 17 are packaged,
one file per fit, sharing this vignette.

```{r fits}
fits <- tibble::tribble(
  ~medium, ~index,       ~endpoint, ~r2,
  "camhb", "cmaxmic",    "dlogcfu", 0.846,
  "camhb", "cmaxmic",    "aubkc",   0.934,
  "camhb", "aucmic",     "dlogcfu", 0.951,
  "camhb", "aucmic",     "aubkc",   0.958,
  "camhb", "tmic",       "dlogcfu", 0.949,
  "camhb", "tmic",       "aubkc",   0.981,
  "shu",   "cmaxmic",    "dlogcfu", 0.985,
  "shu",   "cmaxmic",    "aubkc",   0.965,
  "shu",   "aucmic",     "dlogcfu", 0.982,
  "shu",   "aucmic",     "aubkc",   0.972,
  "shu",   "tmic",       "dlogcfu", 0.735,
  "shu",   "tmic",       "aubkc",   0.849,
  "shu",   "cmaxmicshu", "dlogcfu", 0.972,
  "shu",   "cmaxmicshu", "aubkc",   0.951,
  "shu",   "aucmicshu",  "aubkc",   0.950,
  "shu",   "tmicshu",    "dlogcfu", 0.943,
  "shu",   "tmicshu",    "aubkc",   0.943
) |>
  mutate(
    fit = paste(medium, index, endpoint, sep = "_"),
    stem = paste0("Qi_2026_nemonoxacin_", fit)
  )

index_lab <- c(
  cmaxmic = "Cmax/MIC", aucmic = "AUC0-24/MIC", tmic = "%T>MIC",
  cmaxmicshu = "Cmax/MICSHU", aucmicshu = "AUC0-24/MICSHU", tmicshu = "%T>MICSHU"
)
endpoint_lab <- c(dlogcfu = "Delta log10 CFU", aubkc = "AUBKC")
medium_lab <- c(camhb = "CAMHB", shu = "SHU pH 6.5")

fits |>
  transmute(
    `Model file` = paste0("`", stem, "`"),
    Medium = medium_lab[medium],
    `PK/PD index` = index_lab[index],
    Endpoint = endpoint_lab[endpoint],
    `R^2` = r2
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Qi_2026_nemonoxacin_camhb_aucmic_dlogcfu"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01368-25> (PMCID: PMC13321827, open access)

AUC0-24/MIC is the paper's selected index: it has the highest Delta log10 CFU
R^2 among the CAMHB-MIC indices in both media (0.951 in CAMHB, 0.982 in SHU),
and its targets drive the paper's probability-of-target-attainment analysis.

```{r description, results = "asis"}
cat(
  "**`Qi_2026_nemonoxacin_camhb_aucmic_dlogcfu`** -- ",
  rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Qi_2026_nemonoxacin_camhb_aucmic_dlogcfu"))$description,
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

## How exposure enters

None of the files has a PK component: Qi 2026 analysed the flask concentrations
non-compartmentally and published no structural model of the apparatus.
Exposure therefore enters as covariates, which each model combines into its
index:

| Index | Covariates | Formed in `model()` as |
|---|---|---|
| Cmax/MIC | `CMAX_NEMONOXACIN` (mg/L), `MIC` (mg/L) | `CMAX_NEMONOXACIN / MIC` |
| AUC0-24/MIC | `AUC_NEMONOXACIN` (mg*h/L), `MIC` (mg/L) | `AUC_NEMONOXACIN / MIC` |
| %T>MIC | `FTMIC_NEMONOXACIN` (percent) | used directly |
| Cmax/MICSHU | `CMAX_NEMONOXACIN`, `MIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE` (mg/L) | `CMAX_NEMONOXACIN / MIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE` |
| AUC0-24/MICSHU | `AUC_NEMONOXACIN`, `MIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE` | `AUC_NEMONOXACIN / MIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE` |
| %T>MICSHU | `FTMIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE_NEMONOXACIN` (percent) | used directly |

`MIC` is always the standard CAMHB broth-microdilution MIC, even in the SHU
fits labelled "Cmax/MIC" and "AUC0-24/MIC"; `MIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE` is the MIC
measured with CAMHB replaced by SHU at pH 6.5.

The Delta log10 CFU models integrate a bacterial density `bact` from the
nominal 1e6 CFU/mL inoculum and return `log_cfu`; the AUBKC models are
algebraic and return `auc_log_cfu`.

# Population

The models are in vitro. Twelve clinical *E. coli* isolates (five producing
extended-spectrum beta-lactamase) and the control strain ATCC 25922 were tested
for susceptibility in CAMHB and in SHU at pH 5.6, 6.0 and 6.5 (Table S3); two
further isolates, NTU-001 and NTU-002, joined the high-exposure SHU arm.
Nemonoxacin MICs were 0.5-128 mg/L in CAMHB for the clinical isolates and rose
in SHU by on average 5 +/- 2, 4 +/- 2 and 2 +/- 1 log2 dilutions at pH 5.6, 6.0
and 6.5.

The flask was inoculated at 1e6 CFU/mL, preincubated 1 h at 35 C, and pumped
to reproduce day-10 urine concentrations after oral 500 mg once daily in healthy
Chinese volunteers (Table 1): the Table 1 interval **minimum** concentrations
defined the low-exposure arm and the interval **medians** the high-exposure arm.
Concentrations and viable counts were sampled at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h.

```{r isolates}
# Qi 2026 Table S3, nemonoxacin columns used by the models (mg/L).
# "<0.03" for ATCC 25922 in CAMHB is entered at the censoring limit.
isolates <- tibble::tribble(
  ~isolate,      ~esbl,   ~mic_camhb, ~mic_shu65,
  "21-W031-023", "ESBL+",   4,         16,
  "21-W033-001", "ESBL+",   0.5,        2,
  "21-W035-079", "ESBL+",   8,         32,
  "21-W049-099", "ESBL+",  32,        128,
  "21-W061-049", "ESBL+",   2,         16,
  "21-W031-028", "ESBL-",   1,          4,
  "21-W041-052", "ESBL-",   1,          2,
  "21-W042-007", "ESBL-",  16,         64,
  "21-W049-080", "ESBL-",   2,          8,
  "21-W049-027", "ESBL-",  16,         64,
  "ATCC 25922",  "-",       0.03,       0.5,
  "NTU-001",     "",        1,         64,
  "NTU-002",     "",      128,        512
)
isolates |>
  rename(
    Isolate = isolate, Type = esbl,
    `MIC, CAMHB (mg/L)` = mic_camhb, `MIC, SHU pH 6.5 (mg/L)` = mic_shu65

```

str(p[c("species", "medium", "experimental_arms", "dose_range")], max.level = 1, width = 78)

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `effect = e0 - emax * X^hill / (X^hill + ec50^hill)` | n/a | Methods, PK/PD index and targets, sigmoid Emax equation (equation image 2) |
| `le0`, `lemax`, `lec50`, `lhill` of each file | per file | Table 2, the row named by the file (medium / PK/PD index / PD endpoint); columns E0, Emax, EC50 and gamma |
| `lec50` of the four `tmic` and two `tmicshu` files | Table 2 EC50 x 100 | Table 2 prints the fraction-scale EC50; the x-axes of Figure 6 run 0-1 |
| `log10_cfu0` (Delta log10 CFU files) | 6 | Methods, In vitro UTIs model: "inoculated at 1 x 10^6 CFU/mL" |
| `d/dt(bact) = ln(10) * (effect / 24) * bact` | n/a | Construction that reproduces the Methods endpoint "changes in log10 CFU/mL between 24 and 0 h" at 24 h |
| `addSd` (all 17) | 0 | Not reported; Table 2 gives R^2 only |
| `MIC`, `MIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE` | per isolate | Table S3, NEN columns CAMHB and SHU-pH6.5 |
| Stasis and kill targets | Table 2 | Table 2 columns "Stasis effect" and "Bactericidal effect"; Results, PK/PD analysis |
| Simulated urine exposure | Table 1 | Table 1, Median and Minimum columns |

# The 17 fits

```{r solve-helper}
models <- setNames(lapply(fits$stem, readModelDb), fits$fit)

# The models carry no between-isolate variability by design, so rxode2's
# "multi-subject simulation without omega" warning is expected; muffle only it.
rx_solve <- function(mod, ev) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

# Solve one model at a vector of index values x. For a ratio index the MIC is
# set to 1 mg/L so the exposure covariate equals the index; %T>MIC indices are
# supplied directly in percent. Returns the model's endpoint: the 0-24 h change
# in log_cfu for Delta log10 CFU files, auc_log_cfu for AUBKC files.
solve_index <- function(fit, x) {
  f <- fits[fits$fit == fit, ]
  obs_t <- if (f$endpoint == "dlogcfu") c(0, 24) else 24
  ev <- expand.grid(time = obs_t, id = seq_along(x))
  ev$evid <- 0
  ev$amt <- 0
  xi <- x[ev$id]
  covs <- switch(f$index,
    cmaxmic = list(CMAX_NEMONOXACIN = xi, MIC = 1),
    aucmic = list(AUC_NEMONOXACIN = xi, MIC = 1),
    tmic = list(FTMIC_NEMONOXACIN = xi),
    cmaxmicshu = list(CMAX_NEMONOXACIN = xi, MIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE = 1),
    aucmicshu = list(AUC_NEMONOXACIN = xi, MIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE = 1),
    tmicshu = list(FTMIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE_NEMONOXACIN = xi)
  )
  for (nm in names(covs)) ev[[nm]] <- covs[[nm]]
  out <- rx_solve(models[[fit]], ev)
  # rxSolve drops the id column when only one subject is solved.
  if (!"id" %in% names(out)) out$id <- 1L
  if (f$endpoint == "dlogcfu") {
    w <- out |>
      group_by(id) |>
      summarise(y = log_cfu[time == 24] - log_cfu[time == 0], .groups = "drop")
    y <- w$y[order(w$id)]
  } else {
    y <- out$auc_log_cfu[order(out$id)]
  }
  stopifnot(length(y) == length(x), !anyNA(y))
  y
}
```

## Replicating Figure 6

The x-axis limits follow the panels of Figure 6; the %T>MIC indices are shown in
percent, the scale of the packaged covariates (Figure 6 plots fractions, 0-1).

```{r figure-6, fig.height = 9, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 6 of Qi 2026: sigmoid Emax curves of the 17 Table 2 fits, (a) CAMHB and (b) SHU."}
xmax <- c(
  camhb_aucmic = 250, camhb_cmaxmic = 20, camhb_tmic = 100,
  shu_aucmic = 5000, shu_cmaxmic = 500, shu_tmic = 100,
  shu_aucmicshu = 250, shu_cmaxmicshu = 20, shu_tmicshu = 100
)
curves <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(fits)), function(i) {
  f <- fits[i, ]
  x <- seq(0, xmax[[paste(f$medium, f$index, sep = "_")]], length.out = 151)
  tibble(fit = f$fit, medium = f$medium, index = f$index, endpoint = f$endpoint,
         x = x, y = solve_index(f$fit, x))
}) |> bind_rows()

ggplot(curves, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ factor(medium_lab[medium], levels = medium_lab) +
      factor(index_lab[index], levels = unique(index_lab)) +
      factor(endpoint_lab[endpoint], levels = endpoint_lab),
    scales = "free", ncol = 4
  ) +
  labs(x = "PK/PD index (%T>MIC indices in percent)", y = "Delta log10 CFU/mL or AUBKC",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Qi 2026 (curves only; the observed points are not tabulated).") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

The plateaus agree with the panels of Figure 6 read by eye: for example the CAMHB
AUC/MIC curves level off near -1.85 log10 CFU/mL and 85 log10 CFU/mL*h, and the
SHU AUC/MIC curves near -3.5 log10 CFU/mL and 53 log10 CFU/mL*h. In the
%T>MIC panels with an EC50 above 100 percent (SHU %T>MIC and %T>MICSHU, and
CAMHB %T>MIC for AUBKC) the curve is still falling at 100 percent, as it is in
the figure.

## Validation gate: the published PK/PD targets

Table 2 prints, in columns separate from the parameters, the AUC0-24/MIC values
needed for stasis and for 1-, 2- and 3-log10 kill (Delta log10 CFU = 0, -1,
-2, -3), and for the AUBKC endpoint the values at 50 percent (EC50) and 90
percent (EC90) of the maximum effect. Inverting the packaged models must return
them.

```{r target-gate}
invert <- function(fit, target, upper) {
  uniroot(function(x) solve_index(fit, x) - target, c(1e-6, upper), tol = 1e-8)$root
}
# AUBKC level at a fraction p of the maximum effect: E0 - p * Emax.
aubkc_at <- function(fit, p) {
  th <- rxode2::rxode(models[[fit]])$theta
  exp(th[["le0"]]) - p * exp(th[["lemax"]])
}

targets <- tibble::tribble(
  ~fit,                    ~what,               ~level,                              ~published,
  "camhb_aucmic_dlogcfu",  "stasis (E = 0)",     0,                                   41.6,
  "camhb_aucmic_dlogcfu",  "1-log kill (E = -1)", -1,                                 46.5,
  "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",    "stasis (E = 0)",     0,                                   165,
  "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",    "1-log kill (E = -1)", -1,                                 199,
  "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",    "2-log kill (E = -2)", -2,                                 246,
  "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",    "3-log kill (E = -3)", -3,                                 358,
  "camhb_aucmic_aubkc",    "EC50",               aubkc_at("camhb_aucmic_aubkc", 0.5), 18.5,
  "camhb_aucmic_aubkc",    "EC90",               aubkc_at("camhb_aucmic_aubkc", 0.9), 68.2,
  "shu_aucmic_aubkc",      "EC50",               aubkc_at("shu_aucmic_aubkc", 0.5),   139,
  "shu_aucmic_aubkc",      "EC90",               aubkc_at("shu_aucmic_aubkc", 0.9),   499
)
targets$model <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(targets)), function(i) {
  invert(targets$fit[i], targets$level[i], 1e4)
}, numeric(1))
targets <- targets |> mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model / published - 1))

targets |>
  mutate(model = round(model, 1), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 2)) |>
  rename(Fit = fit, Target = what, `Published AUC0-24/MIC (h)` = published,
         `Packaged model (h)` = model, `Difference (%)` = pct_diff) |>
  select(-level) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Both sides are transcribed numbers and the solve is deterministic, so the
# bound only has to absorb the rounding of the three-significant-figure
# parameters. One wrong digit in E0, Emax, EC50 or H moves these far beyond 1%.
stopifnot(all(abs(targets$pct_diff) < 1))
```

All ten published targets are reproduced to within 1%. The largest gap, 46.2
versus 46.5 for the CAMHB 1-log kill, comes from the rounding of the printed
parameters: with H = 9.98 the curve is so steep that the third significant
figure of EC50 moves the target by about that much.

## Validation gate: structural behaviour

```{r structure-gate}
chk <- curves |>
  group_by(fit) |>
  summarise(
    monotone = all(diff(y) <= 1e-9),
    at_zero = first(y),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    tibble(fit = fits$fit, e0 = vapply(fits$fit, function(f) {
      exp(rxode2::rxode(models[[f]])$theta[["le0"]])
    }, numeric(1))),
    by = "fit"
  )
# Every fit starts at its drug-free E0 and falls monotonically with exposure.
stopifnot(all(chk$monotone), all(abs(chk$at_zero - chk$e0) < 1e-3))

# The %T>MIC rescaling: at an index equal to the packaged EC50 the effect is
# exactly half of Emax below E0. Checked on the algebraic AUBKC fits; for the
# SHU %T>MIC Delta log10 CFU fits the half-maximal change (-13 and -31 log10)
# lies below the 1 CFU/mL floor of log_cfu.
half <- vapply(fits$fit[fits$index %in% c("tmic", "tmicshu") & fits$endpoint == "aubkc"], function(f) {
  th <- rxode2::rxode(models[[f]])$theta
  (exp(th[["le0"]]) - solve_index(f, exp(th[["lec50"]]))) / exp(th[["lemax"]])
}, numeric(1))
stopifnot(all(abs(half - 0.5) < 1e-3))
```

# Simulated urine exposure and the isolates of Figure 5

Qi 2026 does not tabulate the AUC0-24 or Cmax achieved in each experiment, but
Table 1 gives the target urine profile. Weighting each interval concentration by
its duration gives an approximate AUC0-24 for each arm; the 0-2 h interval
concentration approximates Cmax.

```{r exposure}
tab1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~start, ~end, ~median, ~minimum,
  0,      2,    535.34,  150.76,
  2,      4,    176.6,    99.88,
  4,      8,    201.81,   50.49,
  8,      12,   127.45,   50.44,
  12,     24,   90.16,    48.11
)
auc_high <- sum((tab1$end - tab1$start) * tab1$median)
auc_low <- sum((tab1$end - tab1$start) * tab1$minimum)
cat(sprintf("Approximate AUC0-24: low exposure %.0f mg*h/L, high exposure %.0f mg*h/L\n",
            auc_low, auc_high))

# Consistency with the Figure 6 axes, read by eye: the largest CAMHB AUC/MIC
# point is near 200 (low exposure, lowest MIC in the CAMHB arm, 8 mg/L) and the
# largest SHU AUC/MIC point is near 4100 (high exposure, NTU-001, MIC 1 mg/L).
# Loose bounds: the achieved exposure differs from the Table 1 target by the
# Figure 4 calibration slope (0.93 in CAMHB, 1.05 in SHU).
stopifnot(
  auc_low / 8 > 150, auc_low / 8 < 250,
  auc_high / 1 > 3000, auc_high / 1 < 5000
)
```

These ratios fall where the right-most points of Figure 6 sit, which supports
splitting the indices into an absolute exposure and the Table S3 MIC.

The arms of Figure 5 can then be run through the AUC0-24/MIC Delta log10 CFU
models. The time course between 0 and 24 h is the uniform construction of the
model, not the observed kill curve, which fell within 2-4 h and then regrew.

```{r figure-5-arms, fig.cap = "Model-predicted log10 CFU/mL for the isolates of Figure 5 at the approximate Table 1 exposures (AUC0-24/MIC Delta log10 CFU fits). Only the 24 h value is a model prediction of the paper's endpoint."}
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                  ~fit,                   ~auc,     ~isolate,
  "CAMHB, low exposure", "camhb_aucmic_dlogcfu", auc_low,  "21-W035-079",
  "CAMHB, low exposure", "camhb_aucmic_dlogcfu", auc_low,  "21-W049-027",
  "CAMHB, low exposure", "camhb_aucmic_dlogcfu", auc_low,  "21-W042-007",
  "CAMHB, low exposure", "camhb_aucmic_dlogcfu", auc_low,  "21-W049-099",
  "SHU, low exposure",   "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",   auc_low,  "21-W049-080",
  "SHU, low exposure",   "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",   auc_low,  "21-W031-023",
  "SHU, low exposure",   "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",   auc_low,  "21-W035-079",
  "SHU, low exposure",   "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",   auc_low,  "21-W042-007",
  "SHU, high exposure",  "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",   auc_high, "21-W035-079",
  "SHU, high exposure",  "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",   auc_high, "21-W042-007",
  "SHU, high exposure",  "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",   auc_high, "NTU-001",
  "SHU, high exposure",  "shu_aucmic_dlogcfu",   auc_high, "NTU-002"
) |>
  left_join(isolates |> select(isolate, mic_camhb), by = "isolate") |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

grid <- c(0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24)
tc <- lapply(split(arms, arms$fit), function(a) {
  ev <- expand.grid(time = grid, id = a$id)
  ev$evid <- 0
  ev$amt <- 0
  ev <- ev |> left_join(a |> select(id, AUC_NEMONOXACIN = auc, MIC = mic_camhb), by = "id")
  out <- rx_solve(models[[a$fit[1]]], ev)
  out |> left_join(a |> select(id, arm, isolate), by = "id")
}) |> bind_rows()

ggplot(tc, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = isolate)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "log10 CFU/mL", colour = "Isolate") +
  theme_minimal()

d24 <- tc |>
  group_by(arm, isolate) |>
  summarise(delta = log_cfu[time == 24] - log_cfu[time == 0], .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(arms |> select(arm, isolate, auc, mic_camhb), by = c("arm", "isolate")) |>
  mutate(index = auc / mic_camhb)
d24 |>
  transmute(Arm = arm, Isolate = isolate, `AUC0-24/MIC (h)` = round(index, 1),
            `Predicted Delta log10 CFU/mL` = round(delta, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()

pred <- function(a, i) d24$delta[d24$arm == a & d24$isolate == i]
# Results: W042-007 under low exposure in SHU "by 24 h was close to the
# control", and NTU-002 under high exposure ended with "24-h counts similar to
# control". Both are predicted to grow, against a drug-free 24 h change of 2.72.
stopifnot(
  pred("SHU, low exposure", "21-W042-007") > 1.5,
  pred("SHU, high exposure", "NTU-002") > 2.5
)
# Results: W035-079, W042-007 and NTU-001 under high exposure in SHU "showed
# sustained reductions"; all three are predicted to fall by more than 1 log10.
stopifnot(all(d24$delta[d24$arm == "SHU, high exposure" &
                          d24$isolate != "NTU-002"] < -1))
```

The isolate-level pattern follows Results. Under high exposure in SHU the three
lower-MIC isolates fall and NTU-002 (CAMHB MIC 128 mg/L) grows almost as the
control does; under low exposure in SHU, W042-007 (CAMHB MIC 16 mg/L) also
grows, as Results reports ("by 24 h was close to the control"). The predicted
kill for the other low-exposure isolates (up to about 3.5 log10) is larger than
the "primarily bacteriostatic" changes of at most 1 log10 that Results
describes for those arms: each fit pools all arms and isolates, so its
typical-value prediction for one isolate is not expected to match one time-kill
curve.

# PKNCA

There is no PKNCA section. Qi 2026 published no structural PK model of the
apparatus, so none of the 17 files simulates a concentration, and the PK/PD
indices enter as covariates. The exposure arithmetic above is the substitute
check on the PK side.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **%T>MIC on the percent scale.** Qi 2026 fits every %T>MIC index on the
  0-1 fraction scale. The packaged EC50 values are the Table 2 values multiplied
  by 100 (48.7, 479, 129 and 128 percent for %T>MIC; 168 and 109 percent for
  %T>MICSHU) so the covariates are supplied in percent, the convention of the
  `FTMIC_<DRUG>` family. The rescaling is exact, as the structural gate above
  confirms.
* **Indices split into exposure and MIC.** Because every isolate's MIC is
  reported (Table S3) and those MICs reproduce the index ranges of Figure 6,
  the ratio indices are formed inside `model()` from an absolute exposure
  (`AUC_NEMONOXACIN`, `CMAX_NEMONOXACIN`) and an MIC covariate (`MIC` for the
  CAMHB MIC, `MIC_SYNTHETIC_URINE` for the SHU pH 6.5 MIC), so a user can
  re-target a model to another isolate.
* **Delta log10 CFU as an ODE.** The paper's endpoint is the 0-24 h change. The
  Delta log10 CFU files spread that change evenly across 24 h from the nominal
  1e6 CFU/mL inoculum (`log10_cfu0` = 6), so the 24 h value is the paper's model
  and the intermediate time course is a construction. A 1 CFU/mL floor in
  `log_cfu <- log10(bact + 1)` keeps the logarithm finite; it changes the 24 h
  change by less than 0.001 log10 for any change above -3 log10.
* **AUBKC.** Taken as the area under the log10 CFU/mL curve over 0-24 h without
  baseline subtraction, consistent with the drug-free E0 of 192-208 log10
  CFU/mL*h (a mean of about 8.6 log10 CFU/mL). The output is `auc_log_cfu`.
* **No variability.** Table 2 gives point estimates and R^2 only; there are no
  standard errors, no between-isolate variability and no residual SD. Every
  `addSd` is held at 0 and the models are for typical-value simulation. The fits
  pool all isolates and experiments; the number of experiments behind each fit
  is not stated.
* **Exposure in the illustration is approximate.** The per-experiment AUC0-24
  and Cmax were not published; the Table 1 interval-weighted values used above
  are approximations of the target profile.
* **Probability of target attainment not reproduced.** Figure 7 and the
  cumulative fraction of response come from a Monte Carlo simulation of 5,000
  virtual patients whose PK distribution is not reported, so they cannot be
  rebuilt here.

## Errata in the source

* **One of the 18 fits is missing.** Table 2 and Figure 6 both omit the
  AUC0-24/MICSHU fit for Delta log10 CFU (the SHU block has 11 rows, not 12, and
  Figure 6(b) has 11 panels). Only the 17 reported fits are packaged.
* **Figure 6(b), "Delta log10 CFU vs %T>MIC".** The panel's x-axis runs 0-500
  and its curve has the same shape as the Cmax/MIC panel beside it, whereas the
  index is bounded by 1 and the Table 2 parameters for that row (Emax 66.6,
  EC50 1.29, H 9.95) describe a curve that is still near E0 at 0.8 and reaches
  -2.2 log10 at 1. The panel appears to repeat the Cmax/MIC data. The Table 2
  parameters are packaged. This is also the weakest fit in Table 2 (R^2 =
  0.735), and its Emax and the Emax of the SHU %T>MIC AUBKC fit (1425) are
  extrapolations far beyond the attainable range of the index.
* **Target values in the text.** Results gives the CAMHB stasis target as 41.7,
  Table 2 as 41.6 (the parameters give 41.6). The Discussion gives the CAMHB
  1-log10 target as 46.9; Table 2, the Abstract and the Conclusion give 46.5.
* **Footnote wording.** The Table 2 footnote calls the Delta log10 CFU < -1 /
  EC90 targets "bacteriostatic", while the column header calls them
  "Bactericidal effect".
* **Abstract versus Results.** The Abstract states that 500 mg once daily
  attains 90% PTA up to an MIC of 16 mg/L (CFR 92.1%) with CAMHB targets and
  8 mg/L (CFR 59.4%) with SHU targets; Results gives 32 mg/L (94.3%) and 8 mg/L
  (80.5%) for the Delta log10 CFU targets and 16 mg/L (92.1%) and 2 mg/L
  (59.36%) for the AUBKC targets, so the Abstract mixes the two target sets.
* **Censored MIC.** The CAMHB MIC of ATCC 25922 is reported as < 0.03 mg/L and
  is entered at 0.03 mg/L in the isolate table; it is not used in any
  simulation.
* No erratum to Qi 2026 was found as of 2026-11-21.
